newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO coy on number of bidders for unit.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO coy on number of bidders for unit.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday it could not say if it was negotiating with more than one group on the sale of its MeesPierson investment bank.
Dutch-Belgian banking and insurance group Fortis earlier confirmed it was holding talks with ANB AMRO over the purchase of MeesPierson.
"The only thing we can really confirm right now is that yes, we in talks with them (Fortis). We will not say whether we are in talks with others," ABN AMRO spokesman Jules Prast said.
Analysts valued MeesPierson at up to 2.5 billion guilders.
The Dutch bank on Tuesday said it was in talks on the sale of the subsidiary after being approached by a number of unnamed parties interested in buying MeesPierson.
Analysts have welcomed the prospective disposal because of the overlap in the activities of the parent bank and its unit.
ABN AMRO has expanded in investment banking since the 1992 purchase of London-based securities house Hoare Govett.
